screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial evaluating systemic immunomodulator (inosiplex) for alopecia totalis. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized, placebo-controlled trial evaluating systemic corticosteroid (oral prednisolone pulse therapy) for extensive alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized, controlled, investigator-blinded trial comparing two topical corticosteroid formulations (BVF vs BDL) for mild-to-moderate alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating topical minoxidil for extensive patchy alopecia areata, alopecia totalis, and alopecia universalis. Meets selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating topical minoxidil for extensive alopecia areata with long-term follow-up. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized double-blind trial evaluating topical DPCP alone vs with topical minoxidil for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.

Randomized trial evaluating topical cyclosporine, PUVA, and intravenous thymopentin in patients with alopecia totalis/universalis who did not respond to sensitizing therapies. Meets selection criteria.

This is a within-patient comparison study where different concentrations were applied to different scalp areas of the same patients, not a randomized controlled trial between groups. Does not meet RCT criteria.
Randomized trial evaluating topical cyclosporin A vs vehicle for alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating systemic antidepressant (imipramine) for alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized trial comparing topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon alpha, and their combination for chronic severe alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Double-blind trial evaluating topical cyclosporin A vs placebo for alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating topical clobetasol propionate foam for moderate to severe alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial evaluating systemic prednisone followed by topical minoxidil vs vehicle for alopecia areata including alopecia totalis/universalis. Meets selection criteria.

This appears to be a review/summary article discussing results from multiple studies rather than a single RCT. The abstract mentions \'One study was double-blind\' and discusses \'results of these studies\' in plural. Does not meet RCT criteria as a single trial.

Controlled trial comparing squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil, and placebo for patchy alopecia areata. Appears to be an RCT evaluating topical interventions. Meets selection criteria.
This is a questionnaire/survey study evaluating patient perceptions and illness beliefs, not an RCT evaluating interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a methodological/theoretical paper discussing when RCTs may be unnecessary, not an RCT evaluating interventions for alopecia areata. Does not meet selection criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial evaluating aromatherapy (essential oils) vs carrier oils for alopecia areata. Meets selection criteria.
This is a review/update article summarizing knowledge about alopecia areata, not an RCT evaluating interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a retrospective population-based descriptive study assessing incidence and natural history, not an RCT evaluating interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is an observational study examining prognostic factors in patients treated with DPCP, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
Study comparing inosine pranobex (systemic), diphencyprone (topical), and their combination for alopecia totalis. Subjects were divided into three groups. Meets selection criteria.
This is a review article examining genetic basis of alopecia areata, not an RCT evaluating interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper discussing quality assessment of controlled trials, not an RCT evaluating interventions for alopecia areata. Does not meet selection criteria.
